Entry.name: ic.find
Entry.description: Find first device by display name (Labeler). Optional mode (string): auto (default) — glob if pattern has \ or unescaped *, else exact case-sensitive; exact — full-string exact; glob — * substring (case-insensitive outside escapes), \* literal *, \\ literal \; regex — .NET regex on the whole pattern. A single optional number is networkIndex (default mode). With mode and network, use find("pat", "regex", 2) or find("pat", nil, 2) for default mode. Max 512 chars; bad regex → nil.

Entry.name: ic.find_all
Entry.description: Find all devices; same modes as ic.find. Returns 1-indexed ref_id table.

Entry.name: ic.host_info
Entry.description: Get metadata about the chip's host device. Returns a table with: name (display name), ref_id, prefab_hash, type ('suit', 'toolbelt' for the Survival Toolbelt IC slot, 'scripted_visor', 'circuit_housing', 'tablet', 'motherboard', 'device', or 'unknown'). When the host is worn by a player (suit, toolbelt, or ScriptedScreens programmable visor), also includes wearer (display name), wearer_ref_id, and wearer_prefab_hash for the wearing Human when resolvable; keys are absent if not worn.
Entry.example: local info = ic.host_info() if info.type == 'suit' or info.type == 'toolbelt' or info.type == 'scripted_visor' then print('Worn by: ' .. (info.wearer or 'nobody')) end

Entry.name: tick
Entry.description: Called every game tick. dt is the elapsed time in seconds since the last tick. Define this as a global function for the runtime to call it automatically. Module-level code runs once at startup; tick() runs repeatedly.
Entry.example: function tick(dt) local temp = ic.read(0, ic.enums.LogicType.Temperature) ic.write(0, ic.enums.LogicType.Setting, temp) end

Entry.name: serialize
Entry.description: Legacy persistence callback (prefer ic.persist). Called on save and housing power-off. Return a string or nil. Stored in ic.persist under the hood.

Entry.name: deserialize
Entry.description: Legacy persistence callback (prefer ic.persist). Called after init on load. KV from ic.persist is available earlier at module level.
Entry.example: function deserialize(data) local state = util.json.decode(data) myCounter = state.count end

Entry.name: ic.events.on
Entry.description: Register an event handler. handler can be a function or a string naming a global function. Events are dispatched between ticks. Used for inter-chip messaging, ScriptedScreens UI events, and custom events.

Entry.name: ic.events.off
Entry.description: Unregister the event handler for the given event name.

Entry.name: print

Entry.name: require
Entry.description: Load a library module by name. Searches for modules registered on the same data network. Returns the module's return value (typically a table of functions).
